newsitem.title: UK: Scotch Whisky industry to open talks with Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Scotch Whisky industry to open talks with Taiwan.

text.p: Leaders from the Scotch whisky industry will start two days of talks with the Taiwanese government on Tuesday aimed at getting the UK definition of Scotch Whisky accepted, said the Scotch Whisky Association.

The talks, to take place in Taipei, will also include discussion of the monopoly tax system, which means Scotch whisky is taxed at about 10.30 stg a litre while other whiskies pay only 4.64 stg a litre.

The industry leaders will argue that local drinkers need to be protected from look-alike whiskies that have appeared recently on the market, as a result of the lack of a definition and the tax differential.
In 1995, Taiwan was the seventh most valuable market for Scotch whisky, with shipments worth 86 million stg.
